[quote=vespurias;60788773]The first words out of the symmetrical trio was a polite and even "We thank you for your hospitality and hope great fortune is shared between our nations." They said before introducing themselves.

"I am a secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ethan Ludlows." The brunette middle aged man said, giving a polite nod, "I am here to witness and advice the envoy." He shook the King's hand politely.

"And I am the official diplomatic envoy, Sir Walter Sarsen." The middle man, some ashen blonde and the youngest of the three said, giving a deeper nod almost a bow, "I am honoured to meet you." He shook the King's hand gently.

The man to the right of the King was a greying black haired person, "I am Sir Arthur Melville, I am here to represent and report to the Prince's personal staff. A pleasure." He shook the King's hand firmly.[/quote]
The King, having received their greetings warmly, turned to his personal secretary. "Do-yun, bring in the Bangjja bowl to these respectable men." (Bangjja is a traditional Minhokaen hand-forged bronzeware, given at special events and meetings) Do-yun promptly went to go grab it and brought it on a little red pillow with the King's monogram on it and gave it to the envoy. "This is our token of friendship to you. Please, accept it. We are very happy for your presence here today."

"And now, you may take your seats." the King said. In front of them were 5 chairs, arranged in a circle with paper documents in the middle as well as an official notebook for any changes that might need to be added to the document. The King's royal seal was there, and there was a Victorian era gold nib fountain pen for when the document was to be signed.

"Gentlemen, I would like to discuss the reason why we are both mutually interested in this bloc. Today is the day when we can say "No" to violence, respect sovereignty, defend our countries, fight for what's right, and defend the democracy and spirit of the people that build our nations up. Today, we witness history in the making. Neutrality is the path that we are choosing to take in the face of violence between 2 sides that know nothing but war and violence."

"I would also like to reiterate that we will remain firm in our national agendas and opinions. In the face of any threat, we will never give in, we will never bend our knees to any foreign power or agenda, and we will never surrender." Today, we are witnesses to the fact that we pledge not to engage in merciless killing and violence simply for self benefit.

"If there is anything that your excellencies wish to change, you have every right to emphasize your opinions. Once again, I would like to thank you for your presence. If you wish to state your reasons as to why Eneas wants to take part in the Non-Aligned Bloc, that is also more than appreciated.

The King liked giving inspiring speeches because he felt that was the way to best captivate the attention of an audience.
